def solve_cvrp(instance):
    # Extract instance data
    depot = instance["depot_index"]
    demands = instance["demands"]
    capacity = instance["capacity"]
    matrix = instance["distance_matrix"]
    customer_ids = [node for node in demands if node != depot]
    
    # Initialize unserved customers
    unserved = set(customer_ids)
    routes = []

    # First, build initial routes covering all customers using a greedy approach
    while unserved:
        route = []
        load = 0
        current = depot
        while True:
            # Find feasible customers for remaining capacity
            feasible = [node for node in unserved if load + demands[node] <= capacity]
            if not feasible:
                break
            # Select the next customer with the shortest distance from current
            next_node = min(feasible, key=lambda n: matrix[current][n])
            route.append(next_node)
            unserved.remove(next_node)
            load += demands[next_node]
            current = next_node
        routes.append(route)

    # Improve routes locally by attempting to swap or re-order customers to reduce total distance
    improved = True
    while improved:
        improved = False
        for i in range(len(routes)):
            route = routes[i]
            # Try swapping adjacent customers to see if it reduces route distance
            for j in range(len(route) - 1):
                original_distance = (matrix[depot][route[j]] + matrix[route[j]][route[j+1]] + matrix[route[j+1]][depot])
                swapped_distance = (matrix[depot][route[j+1]] + matrix[route[j+1]][route[j]] + matrix[route[j]][depot])
                if swapped_distance < original_distance:
                    route[j], route[j+1] = route[j+1], route[j]
                    improved = True
            # Alternatively, try to relocate a customer to a different route
        # Repair step: attempt to reassign customers if it reduces total distance
        for i in range(len(routes)):
            for customer in routes[i]:
                # Find best route to insert customer into
                best_route_idx = i
                best_position = None
                best_cost = float('inf')

                for j in range(len(routes)):
                    for pos in range(len(routes[j]) + 1):
                        # Skip re-insertion into the same route at the same position
                        if j == i and (pos == routes[j].index(customer) or (pos > 0 and routes[j][pos-1] == customer)):
                            continue
                        new_routes = [r[:] for r in routes]
                        new_routes[i].remove(customer)
                        new_routes[j].insert(pos, customer)
                        # Check capacity constraints
                        if sum(demands[cust] for cust in new_routes[j]) > capacity:
                            continue
                        # Calculate total distance for the moved customer
                        total_dist = 0
                        for r_idx, r in enumerate(new_routes):
                            route_distance = 0
                            prev = depot
                            for node in r:
                                route_distance += matrix[prev][node]
                                prev = node
                            route_distance += matrix[prev][depot]
                            total_dist += route_distance
                        if total_dist < best_cost:
                            best_cost = total_dist
                            best_route_idx = j
                            best_position = pos
                # Perform move if it improves total distance
                if best_route_idx != i:
                    routes[i].remove(customer)
                    routes[best_route_idx].insert(best_position, customer)

    # Final route ordering based on shortest path heuristic
    # (Optional: further optimization could be added here)
    return routes
